short: The library, the gallery frame and routes, the checks
is: The package's code in four parts: `lib/` is the public entry, `routes/` hosts the gallery, `gallery/` is the frame the pages register with, and `checks/` are specs that guard the package's own shape.
conventions: Specs sit beside the code they test (`*.spec.ts` in node, `*.svelte.spec.ts` in real Chromium); `expect.requireAssertions` is on.

A gallery page registers itself with a `meta.ts` under `routes/components/<slug>/` exporting `meta` (a title and one of the groups in `gallery/groups.ts`); the registry finds it by glob and turns away, rather than throws on, a malformed, duplicate or misplaced one.
The gallery's user-visible words live in `gallery/groups.ts` and the frame; the frame is imported through the `$gallery` alias.

Reserved inside `lib/`: `motion/` (the one place motion libraries may be imported), `lazy/` (the one place heavy libraries load, by dynamic import only) and `styles/tokens.css` (the style scan's one exempt file). None exists yet.
The library exports nothing yet; `lib/index.ts` is the whole public surface.

fs.name: checks/
fs.role: specs over the package itself: the lint boundary rules and the import tiers, declared imports, forbidden server-side and JSX files, the style and network scans (scan/), serve config (loopback serving, and Kit's inline options read so no file renaming, service worker or svelte config file gets in), tsconfig parity with web, workspace shape and the public entry

fs.name: gallery/
fs.role: the gallery frame: the registry (page discovery), page meta, the nav groups, GalleryNav, GalleryPage and GalleryState

fs.name: routes/
fs.role: the gallery host: the layout (header, nav, main), the index and, later, components/<slug>/ pages
